Build and apply an absolute risk model

Source: R/compute_absolute_risk.R
computeAbsoluteRisk.Rd

Estimates the absolute risk of a disease over an age interval for each covariate (and/or SNP) profile. The model combines

  • a model for the relative risks of the risk factors (log relative risks of the design-matrix columns of model.formula, and/or SNP odds ratios),

  • a reference dataset of risk factors representing the population in which the model is applied,

  • the population's age-specific disease incidence rates, and

  • optionally, age-specific competing mortality rates.

The baseline hazard is calibrated so that the model reproduces the population incidence rates, and risks of profiles with missing risk factors are averaged coherently over the reference population.

Usage

computeAbsoluteRisk(
  model.formula = NULL,
  model.cov.info = NULL,
  model.snp.info = NULL,
  model.log.RR = NULL,
  model.ref.dataset = NULL,
  model.ref.dataset.weights = NULL,
  model.disease.incidence.rates,
  model.competing.incidence.rates = NULL,
  model.bin.fh.name = NA,
  n.imp = 5,
  apply.age.start,
  apply.age.interval.length,
  apply.cov.profile = NULL,
  apply.snp.profile = NULL,
  return.lp = FALSE,
  return.refs.risk = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model.formula

A formula such as Y ~ x1 + as.factor(x2) + x1:x3 describing the design matrix of the relative-risk model. The response is ignored. Leave NULL (with the other covariate arguments) for a SNP-only model.

model.cov.info

A list with one element per covariate of model.formula, each a list with fields name (the covariate name), type ("continuous" or "factor") and, for factors, levels (all levels) and optionally ref (the referent level).

model.snp.info

A data frame with columns snp.name, snp.odds.ratio (per-allele odds ratio) and snp.freq (risk-allele frequency).

model.log.RR

Log relative risks of the design-matrix columns (no intercept), as a named vector or a one-column matrix with row names; the names must be the column names that model.formula generates.

model.ref.dataset

A data frame of risk factors for a sample representing the population, with no missing values. Columns are matched to the covariates by name.

model.ref.dataset.weights

Optional non-negative sampling weights of the rows of model.ref.dataset (normalized internally).

model.disease.incidence.rates

Age-specific annual incidence rates: a two-column table (integer age, rate) or a three-column table (start age, end age, annual rate in that age band). Must cover consecutive ages including every year of age used by the risk intervals.

model.competing.incidence.rates

Age-specific annual rates of competing mortality, in the same layouts. NULL means no competing mortality.

model.bin.fh.name

Name of a binary (0/1) family-history covariate, used with model.snp.info to simulate genotypes given family history and to attenuate its log relative risk. NA when not applicable.

n.imp

Number of simulated SNP genotype sets of the reference population (1 to 20).

apply.age.start

Age(s) at the start of the risk interval: a single value or one per profile. Fractional ages are allowed.

apply.age.interval.length

Length(s) of the risk interval in years: a single value or one per profile. Fractional lengths are allowed.

apply.cov.profile

A data frame of covariate profiles (columns matched by name; extra columns are ignored); missing values are allowed.

apply.snp.profile

A matrix or data frame of genotypes (risk-allele counts 0, 1, 2 or NA), one column per SNP of model.snp.info, matched by name when the columns are named after all the SNPs and by position when they are named after none (naming only some is an error). If NULL, all SNPs are treated as missing.

return.lp

If TRUE, also return the linear predictors.

return.refs.risk

If TRUE, also return the risks of the reference population over the first profile's interval.

...

Not used. The removed argument use.c.code is accepted with a deprecation warning and ignored.

Value

An object of class "icare", a list with

  • risk: one-column matrix (Risk_Estimate) of absolute risks;

  • details: data frame with the interval (Int_Start, Int_End), the risk (Risk_Estimate) and the profile (genotypes, then covariates);

  • beta.used: one-column matrix of the log relative risks used (SNPs first; the family-history coefficient after attenuation);

  • lps: one-column matrix of linear predictors (if return.lp); for profiles with missing risk factors, the model-averaged linear predictor;

  • refs.risk: risks of the reference rows (if return.refs.risk).

The attribute "calibration" holds the calibrated baseline hazard: a data frame with the age, the population incidence.rate, the baseline.hazard and the survivor-weighted mean relative risk expected.rr at each age of the incidence table.

Details

Model. The hazard of a person with risk factors \(z\) at age \(t\) is \(\lambda_0(t)\exp(\beta' x(z))\). The absolute risk over \([a, a + \tau)\) is computed over whole years of age \(t\), as in earlier versions of iCARE: $$AR = \sum_t e_t \lambda_0(t) RR \exp\{-\sum_{u<t} e_u (\lambda_0(u) RR + m(u))\},$$ where \(RR = \exp(\beta' x(z))\), \(m\) is the competing mortality rate and \(e_t\) is the time the interval spends in the year of age \([t, t + 1)\): 1 inside the interval for whole-number ages, and the corresponding fraction of a year at fractional ends.

Calibration. The baseline hazard solves \(\lambda(t) = \lambda_0(t) E[RR \mid T \ge t]\), the expectation being over the (weighted) reference population still free of the disease at age \(t\), starting from the youngest age of the incidence table.

Missing risk factors. For a profile with missing risk factors, the risk is \(E[AR(z_o, Z_m) \mid z_o]\): reference rows are grouped into 100 percentile bins of the linear predictor of the observed risk factors, and the risk is the weighted mean, over the rows in the profile's bin, of the risk of the profile's own observed risk factors completed with each row's values of the missing ones. A profile with no observed risk factor gets the population-average risk.

SNPs. SNP genotypes of the reference population are simulated under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium from the allele frequencies (n.imp sets), conditionally on family history when model.bin.fh.name is given, in which case the family-history log relative risk is attenuated by half the variance of the polygenic score. Missing genotypes in apply.snp.profile are handled like other missing risk factors. Results depend on the random number generator; call set.seed() first for reproducible results.

References

Pal Choudhury P, Maas P, Wilcox A, et al. (2020). iCARE: An R package to build, validate and apply absolute risk models. PLoS ONE 15(2): e0228198. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0228198

See also

computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval() for models that change at a cut age, ModelValidation() to validate a model.

Examples

data(bc_data, package = "iCARE")

# Covariates and 72 SNPs, with family-history adjustment
set.seed(50)
results <- computeAbsoluteRisk(
  model.formula = bc_model_formula,
  model.cov.info = bc_model_cov_info,
  model.snp.info = bc_72_snps,
  model.log.RR = bc_model_log_or,
  model.ref.dataset = ref_cov_dat,
  model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
  model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc,
  model.bin.fh.name = "famhist",
  apply.age.start = 50,
  apply.age.interval.length = 30,
  apply.cov.profile = new_cov_prof,
  apply.snp.profile = new_snp_prof,
  return.refs.risk = TRUE
)
results
#> Absolute risks of 3 profiles
#> 
#>   Int_Start Int_End Risk_Estimate
#> 1        50      80    0.10173346
#> 2        50      80    0.09031505
#> 3        50      80    0.16899913
#> Profiles and risks: `$details`; risks: `$risk`.
summary(results)
#>  Risk_Estimate    
#>  Min.   :0.09032  
#>  1st Qu.:0.09602  
#>  Median :0.10173  
#>  Mean   :0.12035  
#>  3rd Qu.:0.13537  
#>  Max.   :0.16900  

# A SNP-only model
snp_only <- computeAbsoluteRisk(
  model.snp.info = bc_72_snps,
  model.disease.incidence.rates = bc_inc,
  model.competing.incidence.rates = mort_inc,
  apply.age.start = 50,
  apply.age.interval.length = 30,
  apply.snp.profile = new_snp_prof
)
snp_only$risk
#>      Risk_Estimate
#> [1,]    0.08822113
#> [2,]    0.10509014
#> [3,]    0.13469787
